Actual Article Body:
Voters are favoring Democrats over Republicans on the economy and cost of living, but large shares of the public say they do not trust either party to solve the country’s problems, according to recent polling.

Thirty-eight percent of registered voters said Democrats would do a better job handling the cost of living, compared with 27% who chose Republicans. Another 27% said neither party would do a good job, according to an Associated Press-NORC poll conducted last week.

Actual Article Body:

The nation’s two largest states by land area gave Democrats a boost in the battle for Senate control Saturday, with candidates in Texas and Alaska hitting 50% or more in new polls.

Both races would represent pickups if Democrats are able to hold on and win on Nov. 3, which is just a month away.

In Texas, Democratic state Rep. James Talarico leads Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton, 51% to 45%, according to a New York Times/Siena College poll released Saturday. President Trump’s approval rating in the state stands at 40%, compared with 57% who disapprove.
